items.body:
### Description

When using a Text input block (displayed as a textarea), I would like the
placeholder to be displayed on multiple lines (e.g. to show a template the
user should follow: "Name: ...\nCompany: ...\nMessage: ...").

Using the HTML entity `
` in the placeholder field does not produce a
line break. Instead, the entity is escaped one extra time and displayed
literally in the placeholder text.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a typebot with a **Text input block** rendered as a textarea
2. In the block settings, set the **Placeholder** to:
   `Line 1
Line 2`
3. Preview the bot and look at the textarea placeholder

### Current vs. expected behavior

**Current:** the placeholder displays literally:

    Line 1
Line 2

(or `Line 1&#10;Line 2` depending on how the value goes through the
settings/variable).

**Expected:** the placeholder should be displayed on two lines:

    Line 1
    Line 2

### Environment

- Typebot version: `[v3.17.2]` (self-hosted)
- Browser: `[Firefox 156]`
- OS: `[macOS]`

items.body:
**Describe the bug**

Creating a second WhatsApp credentials in the same builder session fails with:

```
prisma.credentials.create() invocation: Unique constraint failed on the fields: (`id`)
```

The first creation works. Any later creation from the same page load fails until the page is reloaded.

Root cause: in `apps/builder/src/features/publish/components/deploy/dialogs/whatsApp/WhatsAppCredentialsDialog.tsx` the credentials id is generated at module scope:

```ts
const credentialsId = createId();
```

so it is generated once per page load and shared by every `WhatsAppCreateDialogBody` instance. The id is sent explicitly to `createCredentials` (`credentials.id`), because the webhook URL shown in the wizard needs it before the row exists. `resetForm()` regenerates `webhookSecret` after a successful creation but cannot regenerate `credentialsId`, so the second `prisma.credentials.create()` reuses the id of the first one.

`WhatsAppCreateDialogBody` is also used by the workspace credentials page (`CredentialsCreateDialog`), so the bug shows up there too.

**To Reproduce**

1. Open a typebot, go to Share > WhatsApp (or Workspace settings > Credentials > Add WhatsApp).
2. Create WhatsApp credentials. It works.
3. Without reloading the page, open the dialog again and create a second WhatsApp credentials (different phone number / name).
4. The toast shows `Unique constraint failed on the fields: (id)`.

**Expected behavior**

Each dialog instance gets its own credentials id, and a new one after a successful creation. Creating several WhatsApp credentials in a row works without reloading.

**Proposed fix**

Move the id into component state (`useState(createId)`) and regenerate it in `resetForm()`, the same way `webhookSecret` already is. PR ready, will link it here.
items.title: WhatsApp credentials creation fails with "Unique constraint failed on the fields: (id)" on the second creation in the same session

items.body:
**Describe the bug**

Variables holding an integer above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (16+ digits, e.g. a WhatsApp Business Account ID or any Meta Graph ID) get silently corrupted when Typebot guesses their type.

A variable set to `12345678901234567` becomes `12345678901234568` as soon as it is injected into a Script block, a Set variable "Custom" expression, an inline `{{= =}}` expression, the Chatwoot block, or a block that parses its options with `guessCorrectTypes: true` (Google Analytics, Pixel).

Root cause: two helpers convert numeric-looking strings to `number` without checking the safe integer range.

- `packages/variables/src/parseGuessedValueType.ts` does `Number(value)` and returns the result whenever it is not `NaN`.
- `packages/variables/src/parseGuessedTypeFromString.ts` does `JSON.parse(value)` and returns whatever comes out.

Both go through a float64, so any integer outside `[-(2^53 - 1), 2^53 - 1]` is rounded to the nearest representable double:

```js
Number("12345678901234567") // 12345678901234568
JSON.parse("12345678901234567") // 12345678901234568
```

The HTTP Request block is already protected against this on its own path (`@typebot.io/lib/JSONParse` parses big integers as `BigInt`), so this only affects the two "guess the type" helpers above.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a variable `waba_id` and set it to `12345678901234567` (Set variable block, static value).
2. Add a Script block with `console.log(waba_id)` or a Set variable block with a Custom value of `waba_id`.
3. Run the bot and inspect the value: it is `12345678901234568`.

Same thing with a Google Analytics or Pixel block using `{{waba_id}}` in a parameter.

Unit reproduction:

```ts
parseGuessedValueType("12345678901234567"); // 12345678901234568 (number)
parseGuessedTypeFromString("12345678901234567"); // 12345678901234568 (number)
```

**Expected behavior**

Integers that cannot be represented exactly as a JS number should stay as strings, the same way strings starting with `0` or `+` already do. `12345678901234567` in, `"12345678901234567"` out.

**Proposed fix**

Keep the value as a string when `Number.isInteger(n) && !Number.isSafeInteger(n)`, in both helpers. Values inside the safe range keep being converted exactly as today. I have a PR ready with the change and unit tests, I'll link it here.

Trade-off worth calling out: a script doing arithmetic on such a value (`waba_id + 1`) would now concatenate instead of add. Since the number was already wrong before the arithmetic, a correct string seems preferable to a corrupted number, but happy to discuss alternatives (e.g. returning a `BigInt`).
items.title: Variables with integers above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER get silently rounded when their type is guessed

items.body:
### Description

GitHub sign-in is completely broken on self-hosted Typebot. GitHub has rolled out
RFC 9207 (OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Issuer Identification) and now returns an
`iss=https://github.com/login/oauth` parameter in the OAuth callback.

Auth.js validates this parameter against the provider's configured issuer. Since the
GitHub provider in Typebot has no `issuer` set, Auth.js falls back to its placeholder
`https://authjs.dev`, the check fails, and the callback is rejected.

This is the same breakage that hit Langfuse, oauth2-proxy and Spring Security:
- https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/192143
- https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/issues/13091

### Steps to reproduce

1. Self-host Typebot with `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` / `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` set (OAuth App).
2. Open the builder and click "Continue with GitHub".
3. Authorize on GitHub.
4. Redirect back to the builder fails — sign-in never completes.

### Expected behavior

GitHub sign-in completes and the user is authenticated.

### Actual behavior — builder logs

[auth][error] CallbackRouteError: Read more at https://errors.authjs.dev#callbackrouteerror
[auth][cause]: unexpected "iss" (issuer) response parameter value
[auth][details]: {
  "expected": "https://authjs.dev",
  "parameters": {},
  "provider": "github"
}

### Suggested fix

Set an explicit issuer on the GitHub provider, e.g.:

  GitHub({
    clientId: env.GITHUB_CLIENT_ID,
    clientSecret: env.GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET,
    issuer: "https://github.com/login/oauth",
  })

(or bump `@auth/core` to a version that ships GitHub's issuer by default).
Ideally also allow overriding it via env var for GitHub Enterprise deployments.

### Environment

- Typebot version: <preencha a sua>
- Images: baptistearno/typebot-builder:latest, baptistearno/typebot-viewer:latest
- Deployment: Docker Compose via Coolify
- Auth providers configured: GitHub + Email (SMTP)
- Note: email/magic-link sign-in still works; only GitHub is affected.
items.title: GitHub OAuth sign-in broken — "unexpected iss (issuer) response parameter value" after GitHub enabled RFC 9207

items.body:
## Description
When using a Text Input block with "Allow audio" enabled (with separate 
save-variable fields for the text answer and for the audio URL), receiving 
a voice message via WhatsApp produces a broken media URL and writes it to 
the wrong variable. This breaks any downstream use of the audio (e.g., an 
OpenAI transcription block).

This is NOT related to S3/storage configuration — audio upload and 
transcription work correctly when testing via the embedded web bot. The 
bug only occurs specifically with WhatsApp-received audio.

Confirmed reproducible both on a self-hosted instance (v3.17.2) and on the 
official Typebot Cloud (app.typebot.io), using the "send bot to your 
WhatsApp" test feature.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create a Text Input block with "Allow audio" enabled.
2. Map the audio answer to a variable (e.g. `audio`) and the text answer 
   to a different variable (e.g. `mensagem-inicial`).
3. Connect the bot to WhatsApp (or use the "send to your WhatsApp" preview 
   feature).
4. Send a voice message as the FIRST message in a new conversation.
5. Send a SECOND voice message right after, in the same conversation.

## Actual behavior
- After the 1st voice message: the `mensagem-inicial` (text) variable 
  receives a malformed media URL containing "undefined" as the typebot ID:
  `https://[domain]/api/typebots/undefined/whatsapp/media/[id]`
  The `audio` variable also ends up with this same broken URL.
  Any downstream use of this URL (e.g. sending it to an OpenAI 
  transcription block) fails with a 401 Unauthorized error.

- After the 2nd voice message: a correctly-formed URL (with the real 
  typebot ID) appears — but again in the `mensagem-inicial` (text) 
  variable, not in `audio`. The `audio` variable is never updated and 
  keeps the broken value from the first message.

## Expected behavior
- The audio URL should always be written to the variable mapped to the 
  audio answer, never to the text variable.
- The typebot ID in the generated media URL should never be "undefined".

## Environment
- Self-hosted, Docker, v3.17.2 (baptistearno/typebot-builder / 
  typebot-viewer)
- Also reproduced on Typebot Cloud (app.typebot.io) via the "send bot to 
  your WhatsApp" test feature
- S3-compatible storage (MinIO) correctly configured and confirmed 
  working (web bot audio upload + transcription work fine)
items.title: WhatsApp audio input: media URL has "undefined" typebot ID on first message; second message writes correct URL to the wrong variable

items.body: **Describe the bug** On the "Share" tab of a typebot, the "Your typebot links" card shows the public URL as `{viewer domain}/{slug}`. When the viewer domain (common in self-hosted setups, e.g. auto-generated Easypanel/Docker domains) plus the bot slug together are long, the "Copy" button visually overlaps the slug text button instead of the text truncating/wrapping. Fragments of the slug text leak out from behind the "Copy" button on both sides, making the link hard to read. This appears to be purely cosmetic (the copy button still copies the correct full URL), but it makes the UI look broken. This got noticeably worse after the "Site preview metadata" card was added next to the links card on the Share page, since it halves the available width for the links card. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Self-host Typebot with a long viewer domain, e.g. `https://example-viewer-app.12345.hostpanel.io/` 2. Publish a bot with a reasonably long slug, e.g. `my-long-bot-slug-name12` 3. Go to the bot's Share page 4. Look at the "Your typebot links" card next to "Site preview metadata" 5. See the "Copy" button overlapping/covering part of the slug text, with slug fragments visible behind/around the button **Expected behavior** The link text should truncate with ellipsis (or wrap) and never overlap with the "Copy" button, regardless of domain/slug length. **Environment** - Typebot version: 3.17.2 (self-hosted via Easypanel/Docker) - Affected page: Share tab, "Your typebot links" card **Screenshot** Attached below (domain, slug and bot name replaced with placeholder values of similar length to reproduce the same overflow without exposing real data).
items.title: Copy button overlaps bot slug text on Share page when domain + slug are long (self-hosted)

items.body: **Describe the bug** In my setup, I am integrating Typebot with WAHA. I developed a flow that my clients normally use on WhatsApp. However, after they provide the necessary information, I use a "Jump" block to proceed to another group (though the error persists even without this step). In that subsequent block, there is a message asking "Can I help with anything else?", accompanied by two options. The problem arises when I need to use the `/continueChat` endpoint: the object that should contain that message ("Can I help with anything else?") arrives as an empty message, for no apparent reason. In the preview, everything works perfectly. It is worth noting that I use buttons elsewhere as well, and they work perfectly. It is only this specific case that isn't working, and I cannot figure out why. **To Reproduce** 1. Use a jump block. 2. Send the message and the button immediately after. 3. The message preceding the button must be empty in the request. **Expected behavior** The object of this specific message should include the text, rather than an empty string. **Screen recording**
items.title: Empty string in a message preceding a button

items.body:
Hi Typebot Team,

I'm writing to report a specific bug regarding the "Custom head code" feature in the bot settings. While debugging a custom script injection, we found that the script executes perfectly on the initial, clean page load (SSR), but completely fails to execute when a user refreshes the page with an active session stored in localStorage.

Technical Details: The issue stems from how Next.js handles client-side rendering and hydration. It appears that when the Typebot viewer resumes a session on the client side, the custom script from the metadata is being injected into the <head> using React's DOM diffing (likely via dangerouslySetInnerHTML inside next/head).

Because the <script> tag is dynamically appended to the DOM this way during client-side hydration, the browser's native security model ignores it and refuses to execute the JavaScript payload (as per HTML5 spec for innerHTML script injections). We verified this by inspecting the DOM: the script tag is physically present and visible in the __NEXT_DATA__ blob, but the code inside it never runs.

Suggested Fix: To ensure custom scripts run reliably on both SSR and client-side session resumes, you would need to either:

Use Next.js's native <Script> component (next/script) instead of raw <script> tags inside next/head.
Or use a useEffect hook to manually parse the customHeadCode string, construct a node via document.createElement('script'), and append it to the head/body during client-side hydration.
For now, we had to move our global logic to Google Tag Manager as a workaround, but it would be great to see this fixed natively so the "Custom head code" works consistently across all session states.

Thanks for the great product!

Best regards, Dawid Wachałowicz, gryf.ai

**Describe the bug**
If you create a Jump to a group and provide a specific block, and then delete that block, the id remains. When the user reaches that block, the bot breaks and finishes the session.

I believe this is a bug because the same thing does not happen if you delete a group. The group's id is removed from the Jump.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a new jump to a specific block

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48cb6e78-df0a-4b0f-8e7f-684b46c9ae9c)

2. Delete that block

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7364340-8a18-4789-ad78-985a86db9e45)

5. See that the deleted block's id is still there

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/050e269b-53db-4790-b193-32b18a09899a)

**Expected behavior**
For the deleted block's id to be removed from the Jump, or a warning to be shown when the bot is published.
